title: Interactive TTFT stabilizer: prefetch-policy race causing token throughput drops
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Several customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported intermittent first-token-time (TTFT) spikes and sustained tokens/sec degradation during interactive workloads. Pattern correlated with mixed short/long context usage and model fanout; incidents began after a recent prefetch policy change rolled in across clusters. Symptoms: rapid 2-8x TTFT spikes for 95th/99th percentiles, tokens/sec drops of 30-60% for affected workers, and uneven customer impact (single-tenant Dedicated clusters + a subset of Hosted capacity saw worst effects).
steps_to_repro: 1) Deploy a mixed fanout workload (50% short prompts ~64 tokens, 50% long priming ~3k tokens) against model-variants (quantized + fp16). 2) Enable continuous prefetch and simulated autoscaler loading (20-40 concurrent streams). 3) Observe worker logs: overlapping prefetch and scheduler eviction paths trigger aggressive KV cache churn. 4) Measure TTFT and tokens/s with the supplied harness (link in 'links').
impact_summary: Customer-facing: 4 escalation threads opened (2 enterprise Dedicated customers, 1 hosted scale-up customer, 1 private on-prem pilot). SLA degradation risk for Dedicated customers during peak. Internal: alert storm from per-model latency SLOs and increased tracing overhead; we observed correlated GC spikes due to increased eviction churn when kernels attempted to re-materialize KV entries.
root_cause: Race between the new prefetch policy's aggressive reserve and the scheduler's eviction heuristic for heterogeneous contexts. Prefetch reserved memory for long-context sessions, triggering eviction of recently primed short-context KV entries. When short requests arrived, kernels incurred re-prefetch penalties and serialization delays. Additionally, a kernel-selection fallback path introduced a 7-12ms blocking handoff under contention, amplifying first-token lag.
proposed_fix: 1) Revert prefetch policy flags on critical pools (immediate) and disable the new aggressive reserve for mixed-mode pools. 2) Introduce a lightweight soft-reserve that permits immediate access to recently used KV shards (guarded by age-based windows). 3) Patch kernel-selection handoff to be non-blocking under contentions and add backoff jitter. 4) Add a temporary circuit-breaker for private clusters to prefer short-context priming on mixed workloads.
rollout_plan: Phase A (hotfix): rollback aggressive prefetch across Hosted region-us-central and Dedicated pools within 2 hours of approval; patch and deploy to canary nodes, monitor 5m TTFT and tokens/s. Phase B (stabilizer): deploy soft-reserve and non-blocking kernel handoff to 10% canary, 50% ramp, then full rollout over 24h if metrics stabilize. Phase C (hardening): integrate workload classification in admission controller to pin mixed workloads to topology-aware pools. Prevailing rollback plan included in runbook.
monitoring: Dashboards to watch: runtime/ttft/95/region, runtime/tokens_per_second/worker, kv/cache_hit_ratio, kernel/selection_block_ms. We added an ephemeral alert: if TTFT95 > baseline*1.8 for 10m AND tokens/s drop >25% trigger incident paging. Post-deploy we will capture additional flamegraphs and KV churn histograms for 72h.
customer_comm: Notified affected customers on 2026-03-11 18:12 UTC (support threads #CS-7124, #CS-7131, #CS-7137, #CS-7140). Messages provided: acknowledgement, short root-cause description, mitigation timeline, and request to rerun a short workload verification. Follow-up personalized HT reports will be sent after Phase A results.
